presets.name: The funnel
presets.question: Of the leads we worked, where do we lose them?
presets.headline: lj_worked_close_rate
presets.so_what: Read the biggest drop-off first. Lead → contacted is a rostering problem, contacted → conversation is a messaging problem, conversation → appointment is a rep-skill problem, and appointment → sold is a desk problem.

presets.name: Leads we never contacted
presets.question: Did every lead actually get something from us?
presets.headline: lj_contact_coverage
presets.so_what: This one is on FLWUP, not on the team. A follow-up is scheduled for every lead the moment it is created, so anything short of 100% means sends are being skipped. Leads sold before the cadence opener was due are already excluded, so a fast walk-in close never counts against you. Raise a shortfall with us rather than with the floor.

presets.name: Lead-to-sold trend
presets.question: Is our close rate moving, month over month?
presets.headline: worked_close_rate
presets.so_what: One month is noise. Three consecutive months in the same direction is the signal — and the two cards below tell you which input moved.

presets.name: Leads no rep picked up
presets.question: Which leads did the cadence carry on its own, with nobody stepping in?
presets.headline: untouched_rate
presets.so_what: Not the same question as the coverage card — every one of these leads WAS contacted, by FLWUP. This is about whether a person ever got involved. It is never going to be zero and should not be: the point of the cadence is that a quiet lead keeps getting worked without anyone doing it by hand. Read it for the leads that replied and still got no human, which is where deals die.

presets.name: Speed to lead → close rate
presets.question: What does responding faster actually do to our close rate?
presets.so_what: This is the chart to put in front of a rep who argues about response time. Published benchmark: contact inside 5 minutes converts at 25-32%, after an hour at 3-5%. Show them their own curve, not the industry one.

presets.name: Persistence → close rate
presets.question: How many attempts does it take us to convert, and do we make them?
presets.headline: lj_median_attempts
presets.so_what: Conversion typically needs 6-8 contacts; the average dealership makes two, and 92% of salespeople quit after four. If the bars fall away on the right it is not that persistence stops working — it is that only the hard leads survive that long. Look at whether anyone is reaching 6 at all.

presets.name: When we drop leads
presets.question: Which hours of the day do leads arrive and go unanswered?
presets.so_what: A roster, not a telling-off. If the untouched leads cluster at opening, at lunch or after close, name someone to cover that block rather than asking the team to try harder.

presets.name: Conversations we did not book
presets.question: When a customer writes back, how often do we get them in?
presets.headline: lj_reply_to_appointment
presets.so_what: The purest coaching number on the page — the rep had a live conversation and did not turn it into a visit. Nothing about lead quality explains this one away.

presets.name: Rep scorecard
presets.question: Who responds fastest, who follows up, and who closes?
presets.so_what: The document to sit down with. Each rep is measured against the industry benchmark, not against the rooftop average — a whole team can be behind and still look fine ranked against itself.

presets.name: Rooftop scoreboard
presets.question: How is each rooftop performing on the things that predict a sale?

presets.name: Speed-to-lead league
presets.question: Who is answering leads inside fifteen minutes, and who is not?
presets.headline: touched_15m_rate
presets.so_what: Fifteen minutes is the competitive line. Dealers who beat it close around 50% more of the same leads.

presets.name: Lead source ROI
presets.question: Which lead sources actually convert, and how fast?
presets.so_what: Rows reading "Unrecorded" are leads where nobody filled in "How did they reach us?" on the lead form. Until that habit sticks this chart is a sample, not a census.

presets.name: Model demand
presets.question: Which models are people enquiring about, and which of those close?

presets.name: What we actually sell
presets.question: Which cars leave the yard — and how often is it not the one they came in for?
presets.so_what: Read this against Model demand above. A model that draws enquiries but rarely appears here is doing its job as a hook, not as stock. Rows under "Not recorded" are sales closed before the rep was asked what the customer drove away in; that number should fall to zero over the next few weeks on its own.
